evidence.rationale: Positive group operating cash is heavily supported by payable funding; it is not recurring common cash.
Inventory and receivables consume cash while payables supply substantially more; repeated supplier/project funding limits conversion quality.
Property transfers, distinct EV obligations and residual-value remeasurement introduce timing and estimation dependencies.

counterevidence.rationale: FY2025 operating cash is positive and improves from the preceding year; property advances can be normal project funding. This prevents calling all cash generation fictitious or treating growth capex as a loss.
Recognition policy provides explicit performance/risk-transfer conditions; no evidence here establishes that every contract violated them.

assumptions: No after-tax/NCI allocation or normalized FCFE is invented.

invalidationConditions: Verified project-cohort collection and recurring common-cash evidence could improve the band; material noncollection or contract revisions could worsen it.
